counterfactual_missing_items: Hyper-intense signals in diffusion-weighted images (would support stroke)
Vertebrobasilar artery main trunk occlusion or stenosis (would support stroke)
Dissemination in time and space (would support multiple sclerosis)
decisive_items: Incomplete right eyelid closure with visible sclera during maximal effort
Weak muscle strength of right frontalis and orbicularis oculi
No hyper-intense signals in diffusion-weighted images
response.rationale: R8 is directly supported by classic peripheral facial palsy signs (eyelid closure, frontalis weakness) and electrophysiological evidence of denervation, while the MRI lesion is non-specific and lacks DWI restriction, ruling out acute stroke. R1 (MS) is a plausible alternative given the pontine lesion, but the absence of DWI hyperintensity and lack of dissemination criteria make it less likely. Other candidates (R4, R5, R6) are either too vague, contradicted by imaging, or anatomically implausible.

rejected.why: Neuroma is a non-specific label; the lesion location in the pons is not typical for a neuroma, and no supporting features like contrast enhancement or bone erosion are present.
Stroke is contradicted by the absence of DWI hyperintensity and no vertebrobasilar occlusion; the clinical presentation is more consistent with peripheral facial palsy.
Facial nerve schwannoma would typically involve the nerve along its course, not a dorsolateral pontine lesion; the imaging and clinical findings do not support this diagnosis.
